purpose: Define observable legacy-import acceptance fixtures before implementation; synthetic legacy exports only.

dependencyGateDetails.rule: Until T07 is accepted, only independent fixture/interface preparation is allowed; do not implement T08 production behavior or connect a fake-success backend.

sections: §5.5 丢钥、卸载与备份恢复 gate

fixturePolicy.syntheticInputLocation: fixtures/legacy/ (only generated fake values if physical input files are later needed)
fixturePolicy.integrityRule: Hash only synthetic fixture/export bytes generated by the test. Never inspect or hash the user's live profile. Any migration-integrity work against a real copy requires the user's explicit selection of an isolated copy.
fixturePolicy.duplicateIdRule: Only exact same-source replay/idempotency is specified here. Two rows with the same legacy ID but conflicting payloads within one export have no frozen winner rule and must remain an OPEN QUESTION, not an asserted expected result.
fixturePolicy.statusMeaning: NOT_RUN means no import behavior has been verified. A fixture definition is not evidence of passing behavior.

fixtureFamilies.input: An empty synthetic legacy history serialized using the legacy writer's array format.
fixtureFamilies.action: Run import preflight and import once, then repeat the exact same export.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The first import completes with zero imported items and no new history/saved records. Replaying the same empty export makes no change. The synthetic source bytes remain unchanged.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record import-run outcome and counts, before/after synthetic target state, and source fixture hash; do not access a user profile.

fixtureFamilies.input: A fixed-seed synthetic export with 100 unique, valid legacy items across text, link, and small image examples.
fixtureFamilies.action: Import into an isolated synthetic destination profile and enumerate all resulting history records and legacy ID mappings.
fixtureFamilies.expected: All 100 valid source items are represented once in history with preserved legacy identity mapping and validated item metadata/content. Import does not enable cloud sync or create upload operations.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare source IDs to imported IDs/counts and inspect only synthetic records, import-run counters, sync setting, and outbox state.

fixtureFamilies.input: A fixed-seed synthetic export with 2,000 unique valid legacy items within the applicable canonical limits.
fixtureFamilies.action: Import the export and enumerate the completed destination state; interruption is covered by the dedicated resume fixture.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The import accounts for all source items without silently dropping valid rows, preserves each legacy ID mapping, and reports progress/counts that agree with persisted synthetic state. No sync/upload is enabled.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare exact source/import ID sets, completion counters, import-run state, and outbox/sync state; do not infer performance from fixture size alone.

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic export whose valid legacy items are all pinned, with distinct IDs and stable content.
fixtureFamilies.action: Import and inspect history, SavedItem mappings, and the frequently-used collection independently.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Every legacy pinned item remains represented in history and maps to its own SavedItem and frequently-used membership as required by the task card; repeated import creates no second mapping. No pinned item is silently omitted or merged with a different legacy identity.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare synthetic source IDs, history entries, SavedItem identities, collection memberships, and replay result.

fixtureFamilies.input: Use this fixed synthetic PNG vector: data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVQIHWP4z8DwHwAFAAH/yA9iFgAAAABJRU5ErkJggg== (70 decoded bytes; valid PNG IHDR width=1 and height=1). Set legacy byteSize=1 and width/height=9 to prove metadata is not trusted. Also test invalid base64 and truncation by removing the final four Base64 characters.
fixtureFamilies.action: Import valid and invalid image rows through the isolated fake source/target seam while observing validation before persistence.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The fixed PNG vector is admitted with derived byteSize=70, width=1, and height=1 despite incorrect legacy metadata. Invalid/truncated rows produce explicit per-item errors and do not become usable image records; other valid items remain independently importable. No rejected image bytes are logged or uploaded.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare the exact 70-byte synthetic vector and 1x1 PNG header against derived metadata, then record per-item result/error category, durable target rows/objects, and absence of payload bytes from logs/evidence.

fixtureFamilies.input: The same valid 70-byte PNG payload declared with a data:image/jpeg media type.
fixtureFamilies.action: Run only after the specification freezes whether the declared media type must match the decoded image format.
fixtureFamilies.expected: OPEN QUESTION: do not assert acceptance or rejection until the MIME-versus-decoded-format policy is specified.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record only that this synthetic mismatch fixture is present and gated; do not infer behavior.
fixtureFamilies.gate: OPEN_QUESTION: MIME-versus-decoded-image-format behavior is not frozen.

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic legacy export with malformed top-level JSON, plus a separate export with one malformed item among valid rows.
fixtureFamilies.action: Attempt preflight/import for the malformed container, then import the mixed valid/invalid item export.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Malformed top-level JSON is rejected before a usable import run can alter target data; the source remains unchanged. A malformed individual item is isolated and counted as an item error while valid sibling items remain importable; the report never counts the bad row as successful.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare target state and import-run status before/after each attempt, item counters for the mixed export, and the synthetic source hash.

fixtureFamilies.input: One valid synthetic export with unique legacy IDs, imported successfully once; replay the exact same export and hash.
fixtureFamilies.action: Run import again using the same source identity/content and inspect records, mappings, counters, and destination version.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The repeated import does not duplicate history rows, SavedItems, or legacy ID mappings. The reported import-run state and counters agree with the durable synthetic destination state; no fixed result-enum name is assumed. The synthetic source bytes remain unchanged.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare exact target ID sets, row/mapping counts, import-run records, and source hash before and after replay.

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic export with two rows sharing the same legacy ID but different content/metadata.
fixtureFamilies.action: After the duplicate-ID conflict rule is frozen, run this input and compare the result against that rule.
fixtureFamilies.expected: OPEN QUESTION: do not assert a winning row, merge rule, or acceptance result until the specification defines behavior for conflicting duplicate IDs within one export. This case does not count as passing duplicate-ID acceptance coverage.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record only that the conflict fixture is present and gated; no behavior result is inferred.
fixtureFamilies.gate: OPEN_QUESTION: conflicting duplicate legacy ID policy is not specified.

fixtureFamilies.input: A valid synthetic export with an injected process-stop checkpoint after a known committed item boundary.
fixtureFamilies.action: Stop the isolated importer at the checkpoint, reopen the synthetic destination, and rerun the same import.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The interrupted run is recoverable and its committed rows remain valid; retry/resume completes remaining valid items without duplicating already committed history, SavedItems, or ID mappings. The run reports incomplete state until recovery completes.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare durable synthetic state immediately after restart and after retry against the source ID set and import-run progress; no process-kill or profile path outside the isolated test fixture.

fixtureFamilies.input: A valid synthetic export and isolated destination; inject user cancellation at a deterministic boundary after at least one item is committed and before the final source item.
fixtureFamilies.action: Request user cancel once at the deterministic boundary, then observe the terminal import-run state and synthetic source/target. Do not retry automatically.
fixtureFamilies.expected: OPEN QUESTION: the specification requires a cancellation fixture but does not freeze whether partially committed rows are retained or rolled back, how remaining rows are represented, or the terminal result. Do not assert a terminal state or count this case as behavior coverage until that policy is specified.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record only that cancellation was requested at the stated boundary and preserve synthetic source/target snapshots for later comparison against the frozen policy; do not infer expected behavior.
fixtureFamilies.gate: OPEN_QUESTION: user-requested import cancellation and partial-commit policy is not specified.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T08.md: 完成标准与行为测试

fixtureFamilies.input: An isolated storage adapter that reports full after a deterministic number of synthetic item writes, then becomes writable for the recovery attempt.
fixtureFamilies.action: Import, inject storage-full, inspect the interrupted/partial run, restore adapter capacity, and retry the same source.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Storage exhaustion returns an explicit failure and never reports full import success. Already committed valid items remain intact, failed/unprocessed items remain recoverable through the import run, and retry finishes without duplicates. The original synthetic export is not modified.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare source/target ID sets, row counts, per-item counters, import-run state, and source hash across failed and recovery attempts.
fixtureFamilies.gate: Use only an injected storage adapter or isolated disposable test volume; no live disk-full exercise.

fixtureFamilies.input: An isolated synthetic target with a known pre-import ID set and hash; inject OS-vault-unavailable and target-access-denied cases using a fake adapter.
fixtureFamilies.action: Attempt import in each injected failure mode, then compare the original target and synthetic source to their preflight snapshots.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Import does not report success, replace the existing target, or create an empty target over it. Existing target data and source bytes remain unchanged; the failure is observable and distinguishable from a successful import. No real OS vault or user profile is accessed.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare target file/object identity, known synthetic ID set and hash, source hash, import-run result, and all write/replace calls.
fixtureFamilies.gate: T07 accepted and the isolated fake database/vault adapter is available; no live profile or OS-vault exercise.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T08.md: 完成标准与行为测试

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic export envelope containing harmless marker values in legacy cloud-token/password/tombstone fields alongside one valid item.
fixtureFamilies.action: Import the valid item and inspect destination schema, sync settings, outbox, logs, and returned summaries.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Legacy cloud token/password/tombstone content is not imported or logged. The valid item remains local-only, and migration does not automatically enable sync or upload content.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Search only generated synthetic target/log artifacts for harmless marker values and verify sync/outbox remain inactive.

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic legacy image item whose stored bytes are explicitly a downsampled preview and do not include the original image.
fixtureFamilies.action: Import the record and inspect the resulting image availability and user-visible source description.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The import accurately indicates that the original image is unavailable when only a downsampled legacy derivative exists. It does not fabricate or claim restoration of the original image.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare source fixture provenance and resulting availability indication; no real image or user content is used.

requiredNotRunGates.reason: T08 behavior implementation and execution wait until the T07 dependency is accepted.
Never inspect or hash the live %APPDATA%\ClipNest profile. Any integrity check on a real profile requires the user's explicit selection of a distinct isolated copy.

The task/spec does not define which payload wins when one export contains multiple different rows with the same legacy ID. Do not write a winner assertion until that rule is frozen. Exact same-export replay is covered separately as an idempotency fixture.

T08 requires a cancellation fixture, but the spec does not define the terminal state, counter behavior, or whether partially committed rows are retained or rolled back. Keep the synthetic fixture gated until this policy is specified.

The task/spec does not define whether a Data URL media type that conflicts with the decoded image format must be rejected or handled another way. Do not assert mismatch behavior until this policy is frozen.
Actual import into a SQLCipher profile, key-vault boundaries, restart durability, and isolated-profile recovery require the corresponding T07 accepted implementation and platform validation.

acceptanceReminder: This is preparation only. Fixture definitions and JSON parsing do not verify T08 behavior. Preserve actual profile migration, integrity, SQLCipher, vault, and restart gates as NOT_RUN until the task dependencies are accepted and any required isolated-copy decision is explicit.
